references.cite: Heywood, J.B. (1988). Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals. McGraw-Hill. 2nd ed. (2018), McGraw-Hill.
references.use: Crank-slider geometry (Ch. 2), ideal cycles (Ch. 5), SI and CI combustion (Ch. 9-10), pollutant formation and control (Ch. 11), heat transfer (Ch. 12), operating characteristics (Ch. 15). Simplified thermal-NO rate expression (constants 6e16 and 69,090 K) is in the NO formation section of Ch. 11.

references.cite: Turns, S.R. (2012). An Introduction to Combustion: Concepts and Applications, 3rd ed. McGraw-Hill.
references.use: Adiabatic flame temperature, equilibrium, NOx mechanisms (thermal, prompt, N2O, fuel-bound), CO, soot, pollutant emissions chapter.

references.cite: Lefebvre, A.H. and Ballal, D.R. (2010). Gas Turbine Combustion: Alternative Fuels and Emissions, 3rd ed. CRC Press.
references.use: Lean premixed combustion, NOx and CO trends versus flame temperature and residence time, lean blowout, part-load behavior.

references.cite: Lieuwen, T.C. and Yang, V. (eds.) (2013). Gas Turbine Emissions. Cambridge University Press.
references.use: Emission formation and control in gas turbines, fuel flexibility, measurement and regulation.

references.cite: Glassman, I., Yetter, R.A. and Glumac, N.G. (2014). Combustion, 5th ed. Academic Press.
references.use: Combustion chemistry background (CO oxidation, NOx chemistry, soot).

references.cite: Zeldovich, Ya.B. (1946). The oxidation of nitrogen in combustion and explosions. Acta Physicochimica URSS 21, 577-628.
references.use: Original thermal NO mechanism (O + N2 <-> NO + N; N + O2 <-> NO + O).

references.cite: Lavoie, G.A., Heywood, J.B. and Keck, J.C. (1970). Experimental and theoretical study of nitric oxide formation in internal combustion engines. Combustion Science and Technology 1(4), 313-326.
